How a Village Self-Defence Group Turned Into Nigeria’s New Cross-Border Terror Bridge

In 2017, border villages in Sokoto invited an armed herding militia, Lakurawa to shield them from bandits.

By 2026, that former vigilante force had evolved into one of Nigeria’s fastest-spreading terror threats:
• Taxed Kebbi and Sokoto communities ₦50m ($36,000) in March 2026 just to let clerics preach Ramadan tafsir
• Killed 162 civilians in Woro and Nuku, Kwara State after villages rejected its rule
• Built an active corridor linking Sahelian jihadists (ISGS/JNIM) toward northern Benin and central Nigeria

History’s hardest internal security lesson repeats: when the state leaves a vacuum, outsourced community defence rarely stays defensive for long.

Bandit Infighting Claims Over 40 Lives in Zamfara, Brother of Ado Allero Reportedly Killed

By: Zagazola Makama

A violent internal clash among rival factions of armed bandits in the eastern Mada axis of Zamfara State has reportedly left more than 40 fighters dead, including a younger brother of notorious bandit kingpin Ado Allero, identified as “Senator”.

Security sources and local accounts said the deadly confrontation occurred amid escalating tensions within the armed groups operating in the area, although the exact circumstances that triggered the infighting remain unclear.

Among those reportedly killed was Senator, said to be a younger brother of Ado Allero, one of the notorious bandit leaders operating in the North-West.

The reported death of Senator, if confirmed, could represent a significant development within the network associated with the bandit kingpin, particularly if it deepens existing divisions among armed groups operating across Zamfara and neighbouring states.

Preliminary accounts indicated that the confrontation involved armed elements from within the bandit networks, with casualties reportedly exceeding 40 fighters.

Zagazola report that the disputes over territorial control, disagreements over leadership and competition for resources have contributed to tensions among criminal groups operating in parts of the North-West. 

Further updates will follow as more credible information becomes available.

KATSINA STATE MINISTRY OF INTERNAL SECURITY AND HOME AFFAIRS

PRESS RELEASE
23 - 10 - 2026

Bandits Suffer Heavy Casualties as Hunters Repel Attack in Bakori

The Katsina State Government wishes to inform the public of a foiled kidnap operation in Gidan Wawo village, Kakumi Ward, Bakori Local Government Area.

On 23rd October 2026, at about 0128hrs, intelligence revealed the movement of 26 armed bandits on 13 motorcycles, led by one Isiya Kwashen Garwa, towards Dawan Laila forest in Bakori LGA.

Based on the intelligence, all security assets in Bakori LGA were immediately placed on alert to prevent a planned mass kidnap in neighbouring communities.

At about 1331hrs on the same date, reports were received of an attack in which the bandits burnt a private vehicle belonging to one Jamilu Lawal, aged 50, conveying three others travelling to Illela market in Sokoto State from Kakumi ward.

In swift response, hunters from Gidan Wawo were mobilised and engaged the criminals in a gun duel. The operation led to the neutralization of fourteen (14) bandits.

Regrettably, we lost one gallant community hunter, Mohammed Ibrahim Jidda, aged 29, who paid the supreme price in defence of the community. One other hunter, Usman Sunday, aged 25, sustained minor gunshot injuries and is receiving treatment. One victim, Jamilu Lawal, was burnt to death in the vehicle during the rescue operation, while three other victims were successfully rescued.

Intelligence has revealed plans for a possible reprisal attack by the bandits following the heavy casualties suffered. The state government, in collaboration with all security agencies, has put in place appropriate countermeasures to neutralize any further threats in the area.

The government commends the courage and sacrifice of our security operatives and community hunters and assures citizens that we remain resolute in protecting lives and property across the state.

We call on the public to remain calm and continue to provide timely and credible information to security agencies.

Dr. Nasir Mu'azu
Commissioner for Internal Security and Home Affairs, Katsina State

23 October, 2026

results.title: Lakurawa, Boko Haram and ISWAP do follow jihadist doctrine.
results.description: Lakurawa, Boko Haram and ISWAP do follow jihadist doctrine. In Zamfara the main actors remain profit-driven bandit gangs focused on ransoms, cattle rustling and mining levies from local Muslim communities. Lakurawa is hybrid and expanding from Sokoto/Kebbi with some ties, but the dominant pattern there is still economic banditry.
